title: backlog.py find also names closed items from KB-Work history, so 'file a bug if no item covers it' can be decided by the tool
goal: backlog.py find WORDS also lists items whose files a sprint close deleted, read from git history (the item file at its last commit and the KB-Work commit that did it), marked as closed with their done commit, so a goal clause 'file a bug if no item covers it' finds a defect an earlier sprint already fixed (SP-flkl5gom close: find said no open item held ops_no_work_rows, while BG-ese7wmz3 had fixed it in 9ba285039; the worker found it only by searching git history). A planted test proves a closed item is listed and an unrelated one is not.

run: import subprocess,sys;r=subprocess.run(['python3','_tools/rag.py','pack','--root','_self','does backlog.py find list items a sprint close deleted'],capture_output=True,text=True);ok=r.returncode==0 and 'coverage: good' in r.stdout;print('packs good:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

notes: Checks are planned when a sprint commits it (the planted test the goal names).
